title: 25znbx
The poisoning of Hasan
hook: Imam Hasan made peace so that blood would not be shed. Mu'awiya trampled the condition underfoot and had him poisoned.
scenes.0.text: When **Ali** was martyred in Kufa, the people pledged allegiance to his son **Hasan**. A pledge of allegiance. The Prophet's grandson, who he called "Sayyid", thus assumed the leadership of the Ummah. In his will, Ali left the administration to his son. He didn't say a word about being handed over to the deputy. But Mu'awiya relied on the wealth of Damascus' trade routes and the army he had raised for years. He didn't recognize Hasan and marched with his army on the Kufa. And the army of Kufa soon began to split up because of the commanders who were bought.
scenes.1.text: Betrayal followed treachery within the Kufa army. Ubaydullah b. Abbas, one of **Hasan**'s commanders, left the army one night and secretly went to Mu'awiya. Commanders bought with gold, soldiers scattered in the dark of night. Hasan saw that the loyal friends of the Ahl al-Bayt would be broken in such an army. He stopped the war to avoid bloodshed and left the rule to Mu'awiya. The Prophet said, "This is my son Sayyid. Allah will reconcile the two groups of the Muslims". This peace was not a sign of weakness, but of stopping the bloodshed of the nation in a purchased army.
scenes.2.text: The terms of the peace treaty were clear. The Mu'awiya would judge by the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of the Prophet. He wouldn't insult Ali to anyone and he wouldn't insult him in the pulpit. He would not appoint a caliph to succeed him. With these conditions, **Hasan** wanted to protect the honour of the Ahl-i Beyt, the lives of his friends and the cleanliness of the pulpit. The deputy agreed to all these conditions and the agreement was signed. And the people of the Qufa breathed easy for a while. But the life of the signed document depended on the Mu'awiya's word.
scenes.3.text: Shortly after the peace, Mu'awiya made a speech to the people at Nuhayl near Kufa. He made no secret of his intention in this speech: "I did not discourage you from performing the prayer or fasting. I fought to rule you". Then he said he counted the words he had said to Hasan under his feet. The peace the Prophet's grandson made to prevent bloodshed was openly violated before the ink was dry. The Mu'awiya's main purpose was not to protect the religion of the Ummah, but to rule over the Ummah. And he would make his son, Yazid, the heir.
scenes.4.text: Immediately after the truce, the governors of the Emirate began to curse **Ali** in the minbars at the order of Mu'awiya. **Hucr b. Adi** and his companions, who were friends of Ali in Kufa, objected. Hucr was known for his love for Ali. He paid the price for that love by dying with his friends. **Hasan** had retreated to Medina after the peace. He watched all this happen patiently in his grandfather's hometown. The years of silence in Medina would end with a poison as the terms of peace were broken one by one.
scenes.5.text: Mu'awiya wanted to make his son Yazid his successor. The biggest obstacle was Hasan, who knew the terms of peace and carried the love of the people. Mu'awiya secretly sent word to Hasan's wife, Ca'de bint Esh'as. He promised her that if she poisoned Hasan, he would marry her son Yazid and give her one hundred thousand dirhams. That's a promise he made in California. After Hasan was martyred, Mu'awiya did not keep his promise. Ca'de didn't marry Yazid or take all the money.
scenes.6.text: In Medina, it is said that **Hasan** was poisoned and suffered for forty days. Legend has it that his liver was shattered. This is not a doctor's report, it's an expression of grief. The Katade relates that Hasan said that his liver was broken for him. The Sunni scholar Ibn Abdilberr relates that a group of people attributed the poison to Mu'awiya, but he does not make a definitive judgment. Shiite sources clearly state that Mu'awiya was behind the poison. The grandson, whom the Prophet called the master of the youth of paradise, was martyred in his own home in Medina.
scenes.7.text: Husayn took the body of his brother **Hasan** to be buried with his grandfather, the Prophet. But Aisha and Mervan cut the road. By Aisha's order, arrows were thrown at the coffin of the Prophet's grandson. Before his death, Hasan had made a will that "not a drop of blood be spilled at my funeral". He wanted to be buried in Baku if he got in trouble. Husayn did not draw his sword and turned the coffin into a Baku. Hasan was buried in the Baku cemetery next to his grandmother **Fatima bint Esed**. Thanks to your brother's will, no blood was spilled that day. But Medina never forgot the arrow shot at the Prophet's grandson's funeral.
sunni.0.says: The Prophet calling Imam Hasan «sayyid» and the saying «He will reconcile two great groups».
sunni.1.says: They do not regard the report of Mu'awiya's promise to Ja'da as established; they relate the poisoning as an event.
sunni.2.says: The conditions of the peace, Mu'awiya's entry into Kufa, and the Year of Unity.
shia.0.says: The poisoning, Ja'da, and Mu'awiya's promise.
shia.1.says: The peace conditions, Mu'awiya's speech at Nukhayla, and the poisoning.
shia.2.says: Mu'awiya's view of the conditions and the reasons for Imam Hasan's peace.
shia.3.says: It is reported that Aisha personally prevented the coffin from being buried next to the Prophet and gave the order to shoot, that the men of Mervan shot with this order, that Ibn Abbas spoke of camels and mules and that Husayn buried it in Baku without drawing a sword.
shia.4.says: Hasan's commander was Ubaydullah b. It is said that Abbas passed by Mu'awiya at night.
shia.5.says: The peace conditions and Mu'awiya's failure to keep them.
disputes.0.title: 1jf3g0w
Who poisoned Imam Hasan?
disputes.0.sunni: There are many accounts of Hasan being poisoned. Some Sunni scholars disagree with the Mu'awiya's order, and say that death may be due to illness.
disputes.0.shia: There are many sources that tell of Imam Hasan's being poisoned. Among Shia books, Mufid, Kulayni and Tabarsi relate that Mu'awiya persuaded Ja'da to do this.
disputes.1.title: q0e65r
Were the peace conditions kept?
disputes.1.sunni: It is agreed that Imam Hasan gave up the leadership so that blood would not be shed. The text of the conditions varies; practices such as cursing can be considered to have damaged the spirit of the peace.
disputes.1.shia: It is agreed that Imam Hasan gave up the leadership so that blood would not be shed. In the Shia account, Mu'awiya accepted the conditions intending from the start to break them.
questions.0: When Hasan's army was dispersed, he chose to stop the bloodshed. Why do you think Hasan made it a condition of the peace that Ali should not be insulted and appointed as his successor?
questions.1: After the reconciliation, abuse spread in the pulpits and the succession came up. Why do you think these two practices touched on these two clauses of the settlement agreement?
questions.2: Hasan's poisoning is covered in many books, but the perpetrator remains controversial. Why do you think the fact that the perpetrator was conflicted doesn't eliminate the incident itself?
summary: Mu'awiya was enriched by Damascus' trade routes. I 'm sorry . I 'm sorry . He bought Abbas and his commanders. Hasan ended the war to prevent bloodshed. The deputy violated the terms of the truce. Hasan was martyred by poison around 50 A.H.
key: The conditions of the peace and the poisoning of Imam Hasan
notes.0: Mu'awiya broke up Hasan's army with a bribe. Abbas went to Mu'awiya at night.
notes.1: Among the peace conditions are counted not letting anyone be cursed and not appointing a caliph.
notes.2: It is reported that Mu'awiya said at Nukhayla "I fought you to rule over you" (should be checked against the source).
notes.3: Hasan was martyred by poison around 50 A.H.
notes.4: That Imam Hasan was poisoned is told in the history books; Ja'da's name is mentioned. In the Ja'fari school this is his martyrdom.
